pairs.why: The two saucers are built almost the same, but A's saturated teal body is closer to the strong single-colour masses of the real cards, while B's pale silver looks washed out.
B is a full, solid saucer seen from the side with a clear underside, like the chunky toy objects in the real cards; A is a flat disc seen from above and reads weaker.
B is built like a real astronaut helmet, with ear pieces and a clean white shell; A is a blue-and-orange ball on a plinth that looks like a statue.
A is a plain white sphere sitting on a pedestal like a figurine, while B is a believable, well-built helmet in the real cards' soft, rounded style.
B's navy tube and warm wooden tripod match the wood and calmer colours of the real cards; A's white-and-orange tube on a grey mount looks more like a plastic toy.
A's surfaces are smoother and less speckled, which the lessons show is closer to the real cards, though both are built about equally well.
B's smooth, warmly lit base with a glowing door reads like the real lighthouse and motel cards, while A has the speckled ground the lessons marked down.
A and B are almost the same image, with the same build, palette and texture, so neither is meaningfully closer.
